summary: Payment failures ("ledger write failed: No space left on device") originate in the shared ledger-db, not in payment-service v6.0.0. ledger-db disk climbed steadily from 77.67% at 11:00 to 100% by ~14:54 — well before and independent of the 14:46 deploy — driven by an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining tens of GB of WAL. payment-service errors began at 15:00:26 and, critically, continued unchanged (320 more errors through 16:57) AFTER the v6.0.0 rollback at 15:12, so the rollback did not restore service. The deploy came 14 minutes before onset and is correlational, not causal. Error rate remains ~60% at the latest data.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' on the shared ledger-db retained tens of GB of WAL, filling the data volume to 100% well before the deploy. Once full, PostgreSQL could not write WAL or extend relation files, so every payment-service ledger write failed with 'No space left on device', producing the ~60% payment error rate. The fault originates in ledger-db/infrastructure capacity, not in the application release.

causal_chain.claim: Inactive replication slot analytics_cdc stops advancing, so PostgreSQL retains WAL indefinitely
Retained WAL + normal data growth fill the data volume; disk_used_pct climbs from 77% to 100% between 11:00 and 14:54
At 100% disk, PostgreSQL cannot write WAL or extend relation files ('No space left on device' PANICs and errors)
payment-service ledger writes fail, error rate jumps to ~60% at 14:56-15:00

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' slot belongs to a CDC consumer that stopped/never started, so the slot is the source of the WAL growth (the consumer service is not in the telemetry roster).
No other workload wrote enough to fill the remaining ~22% of disk in the pre-deploy window (consistent with the steady linear climb).

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate-flow release caused the ledger failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The new UPI mandate flow in v6.0.0 introduced a new MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type that writes incorrectly to ledger-db, causing ledger write failures and the 60% payment error rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted on timing and recovery: ledger-db disk was already >90% at 13:10, ~96 minutes before the 14:46 deploy, and the error is a DB-level 'No space left on device', not a schema/entry-type error. Decisively, rolling back v6.0.0 at 15:12 did NOT recover service — payment-service emitted 320 identical disk-space errors through 16:57. A release-caused fault would clear on rollback.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank-partner-api dependency failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank partner API degraded, causing payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: bank_api_error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout, and the actual error text is a database disk-space error, not an API/network error.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config/feature-flag change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A configuration change altered ledger write behavior.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: get_config_changes returned zero changes for all services in the window.

facts.statement: payment-service ledger write failures are 'could not extend file: No space left on device' errors.
payment-service error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~60% starting at the 14:56 bucket.
ledger-db disk_used_pct climbed from 77.67% (11:00) to 100% (14:54) and stayed at 100%.
ledger-db logged an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining up to 92599 MB of WAL repeatedly from 12:19.
ledger-db began emitting 'No space left on device' PANICs/ERRORs at 15:01 and these continued through 16:57.
The only deployment was payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46, rolled back at 15:12.
payment-service errors continued after the rollback: 320 disk-space errors from 15:12:08 to 16:57:54.
No config or feature-flag changes occurred in the window.
A prior incident (HIST-114) had the same ledger-db-WAL-retention signature, categorized resource_exhaustion.

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' replication slot is owned by a CDC/analytics consumer that stopped, and that consumer is the source of the retained WAL.
The deploy of v6.0.0 at 14:46 did not itself contribute meaningful ledger write volume that accelerated the disk fill.

timeline.event: ledger-db disk already at 77.67% and rising ~1%/8min; replication lag ~926ms
First 'replication slot analytics_cdc is inactive; retaining 63157 MB of WAL' warning on ledger-db
payment-service v6.0.0 (new UPI mandate flow) deployed
First payment-service 'ledger write failed: No space left on device' error; error rate ~60%
First ledger-db 'PANIC ... No space left on device' on pg_wal
payment-service continues emitting identical disk-space ledger failures after rollback
Latest data: payment errors and ledger-db PANICs still ongoing

recommended_actions.action: Free disk on ledger-db immediately: drop the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (after confirming the CDC consumer is dead) to release retained WAL.
recommended_actions.rationale: The inactive slot is retaining tens of GB of WAL and the volume is pinned at 100%, the direct cause of all write failures.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the payment-service rollback as the fix; it already happened and service did not recover.
recommended_actions.rationale: 320 errors continued after the 15:12 rollback, so the release is not the cause; effort should go to the DB.

recommended_actions.action: Verify disk recovers and payment error rate returns to baseline after the slot is dropped.
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the causal chain and validates recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on replication-slot lag/retained-WAL size and on ledger-db disk_used_pct (page at ~85%).
recommended_actions.rationale: The disk climbed for ~4 hours with only a soft warning; earlier paging would have prevented the SEV-1. Same gap existed in HIST-114.

recommended_actions.action: Audit/restart the CDC consumer that owns the analytics_cdc slot and add a heartbeat so orphaned slots are detected.
recommended_actions.rationale: Root trigger is an inactive consumer letting its slot pin WAL.

recommended_actions.action: Set a max_slot_wal_keep_size / retention cap and expand or monitor ledger-db volume headroom.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents a single orphaned slot from taking the shared ledger-db offline again.

data_gaps: The CDC consumer service owning the 'analytics_cdc' slot is not in the telemetry roster ('analytics-cdc' is an unknown service), so why the slot became inactive could not be confirmed from logs/metrics.
No ledger-db filesystem metrics beyond disk_used_pct (e.g., absolute GB free or WAL directory size) were available to quantify exactly how much the slot retention consumed.

It is not directly proven from telemetry that ledger/payment writes are the only writer filling the disk in the pre-deploy window; the steady linear climb is consistent with the slot but not a direct measurement.
